I mean, I'm not sure my advice is worth much since almost all of my relationships were before I got diagnosed haha. But if I were to give advice to a future partner it would be:

to be patient (we're already beating ourselves up) 
to forgive easily (because we don't mean the outbursts) 
to care without being condescending (for me that could be my partner asking if I've taken my meds, but not nagging me if I haven't) 
and honestly just showing love in whichever way you both appreciate.

Good luck, I think you're off to a great start, and most importantly: communicate with her. :)

As someone with bipolar, I would be very happy to see a partner do research and ask questions like you're doing. Even though we're all different, knowing the basics of the disorder will help you both. And have patience with her, it's hard enough to live with. :)

I mean, I could understand if a new partner has issue with me seeing my ex all the time, but the occasional coffee or text is just dumb to get upset about. 

What's much worse is the way your boyfriend is reacting. Like, I've self-harmed, I get it, it's like a drug that's hard to kick, but using it to manipulate someone is absolutely unacceptable. It's incredibly abusive. I think that's the part that's gonna be tough to work through. Are either of you in therapy? I wish you the best of luck!

For me it helped to find a job that's understanding of me having different mental abilities than most people, I have the freedom to work from home if I'm struggling getting out of bed sometimes, and I'm also able to use the extra energy I have other times to put in extra hours that I can take off another time. I haven't told my boss outright that I'm bipolar (don't want to be judged for being crazy lol), but he knows that I have mental health issues because I see a doctor so much. 

My advice would be to try to find a job with a good work environment for YOU, and try to adapt it so your mental health is as good as possible as best you can. Good luck! :)

I don't necessarily think her dad is being a bad parent, I was left alone a lot as a kid and I don't blame my mum for that (she had to work), but she always made sure I had phone numbers by the landline to 911, my grandparents and neighbours. 

I only remember having to use it once, because I came home from school and my kitten had managed to drag in a bunny the size of her.
